question: G-trivial replaced the model's hypothesis STEP with a canned string. Was its -36.2 the canned TEXT, or the CHOICE of region? G-trivial' forces the same region but the hypothesis is the MODEL'S OWN, selected from a structural candidate set (one teacher-forced candidate per visible region, greedy always included).
the_answer: THE CHOICE, not the text. G-trivial' lands 2.6 points above G-trivial -- two episodes out of eighty -- and identically on three slices of four.

and_the_instrument_checks_that_make_that.why this matters: identical outcomes from two arms is the shape of a harness bug -- one arm silently running the other. It is not that here: the arms diverge at step 1 in 66 episodes and take different paths in 72. They change the ROUTE and not the DESTINATION.

the_detail_that_strengthens_it: G-trivial's injected action carries task['bug_class'] -- the TRUE bug class. So G-trivial is a STRONGER oracle than 'the naive prior': it is handed both the symptom region and the right class. G-trivial', which must invent the class and mostly writes the wrong one, matches it. Being told the answer at step 1 is worth two episodes in eighty.
candidate_set: structural: k=4 at every decision point, all four regions offered, ZERO fallbacks to greedy. The earlier sampled set offered one region at 40% of decision points and fell back 12 times in 40 -- its apparent 8/20 on slice 1 was the fallback, i.e. the baseline, not the model's text mattering.
bounds: 80 episodes, four slices, one model, greedy decoding.

This is a v1 result and v1's localisation axis is degenerate (v1_symptom_determines_region.json). It decomposes G-trivial's -36.2, which is also a v1 number; it is NOT evidence about G, which runs on v2.
The two differing episodes are slice 4 only. At n=20 per slice that is noise, and the claim is the pooled 2.6 points, not a per-slice ordering.
